source_act: Section 7(1) & Section 19, Right to Information Act, 2005
user_query: I filed an RTI application requesting road repair expenditure details from the municipal corporation, but got no response after 35 days.
legal_text_raw: Under Section 7(1) of the RTI Act, the Public Information Officer (PIO) is statutorily bound to provide information within 30 days (48 hours if life and liberty is involved). Since they failed, you can file a 'First Appeal' under Section 19(1) before the First Appellate Authority within 30 days.

Since they failed, you can file a 'First Appeal' under Section 19(1) before the First Appellate Authority within 30 days.

source_act: Section 20(1), Right to Information Act, 2005
user_query: Can a Public Information Officer (PIO) be personally fined for deliberately rejecting or delaying an RTI query?
legal_text_raw: Yes. Under Section 20(1) of the RTI Act, the Information Commission can impose a personal penalty of Rs 250 per day (up to a maximum of Rs 25,000) directly on the PIO for unreasonable refusal, delay, or providing false/misleading information, deducted from their salary.
layman_explanation: Yes. Under Section 20(1) of the RTI Act, the Information Commission can impose a personal penalty of Rs 250 per day (up to a maximum of Rs 25,000) directly on the PIO for unreasonable refusal, delay, or providing false/misleading information, deducted from their salary.

source_act: Article 21 (Parmanand Katara v. Union of India) & Clinical Establishments Act
user_query: A private hospital refused to admit a road accident victim in critical condition because the family could not deposit Rs 50,000 advance.
legal_text_raw: The Supreme Court in the landmark Parmanand Katara case ruled that preserving human life is paramount. Every doctor and hospital (public or private) has a non-negotiable legal obligation to provide immediate emergency medical aid without waiting for police formalities or advance payments. Refusal is medical negligence.

Every doctor and hospital (public or private) has a non-negotiable legal obligation to provide immediate emergency medical aid without waiting for police formalities or advance payments. Refusal is medical negligence.

source_act: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 & Res Ipsa Loquitur Principle
user_query: A surgeon left a surgical sponge inside my relative's abdomen during surgery causing severe infection and second operation.
legal_text_raw: Leaving a foreign object inside a patient during surgery is a prima facie case of gross Medical Negligence under the legal doctrine of 'Res Ipsa Loquitur' (the thing speaks for itself). You can file a consumer complaint for heavy compensation before the State/National Consumer Commission and an FIR under Section 106 BNS.

user_query: Can a police officer demand money or refuse to return my seized mobile phone after the investigation is completed?
legal_text_raw: No. Demanding money is criminal corruption under the Prevention of Corruption Act. To retrieve seized property (Superdari), file an application before the Judicial Magistrate having jurisdiction under Section 503 BNSS seeking release of the vehicle or phone on furnishing an indemnity bond.

source_act: Section 179, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
user_query: What are the rights of an individual summoned by police for questioning as a witness?
legal_text_raw: Under Section 179 BNSS, males under 15 years, males above 60 years, women, and physically disabled persons cannot be required to attend the police station; they must be questioned at their place of residence. Furthermore, witnesses are entitled to reasonable travel allowance for attending police summons.

source_act: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 & Consumer Protection Act

legal_text_raw: No. Charging above MRP is a punishable statutory violation under Section 36 of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009. Dual pricing for identical packaged goods has been held unlawful by courts and the National Consumer Commission. You can complain via the NCH app (1915) or e-Daakhil.

source_act: Section 7(1) Proviso, Right to Information Act, 2005
user_query: What is the time limit for obtaining information under RTI if it concerns a person's Life or Liberty?
legal_text_raw: Under the proviso to Section 7(1), if the information sought concerns the 'life or liberty' of a person (such as medical emergency, unlawful police custody, or preventive detention), the PIO MUST provide it within 48 hours.

source_act: Section 2(h) & Section 2(f), RTI Act, 2005
user_query: Can private schools or private hospitals be questioned directly under the RTI Act?
legal_text_raw: Purely private entities are not directly 'public authorities'. However, under Section 2(f), a citizen can seek information regarding private schools/hospitals through the government regulatory department (Education Dept, Health Dept) that oversees them.
layman_explanation: Purely private entities are not directly 'public authorities'. However, under Section 2(f), a citizen can seek information regarding private schools/hospitals through the government regulatory department (Education Dept, Health Dept) that oversees them.

source_act: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (Supreme Court of India, 1997)
user_query: What are the landmark D.K. Basu guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court for police arrest and detention?
legal_text_raw: Mandates: 1) Police must wear visible name tags; 2) Prepare an Arrest Memo signed by an independent witness; 3) Inform a relative within 8-12 hours; 4) Conduct medical examination every 48 hours; 5) Allow meeting with lawyer during interrogation.

source_act: Article 20(3), Constitution of India (Nandini Satpathy v. P.L. Dani)
user_query: Can an accused person remain silent during police interrogation without being tortured or coerced?
legal_text_raw: Yes. Article 20(3) of the Constitution guarantees the fundamental Right Against Self-Incrimination ('No person accused of an offense shall be compelled to be a witness against himself'). Police cannot compel or torture an accused to confess.
layman_explanation: Yes. Article 20(3) of the Constitution guarantees the fundamental Right Against Self-Incrimination ('No person accused of an offense shall be compelled to be a witness against himself'). Police cannot compel or torture an accused to confess.

user_query: What is the maximum period an accused person can be remanded to Police Custody under BNSS?
legal_text_raw: Under Section 187 BNSS, police custody can be granted up to a total of 15 days in whole or in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days of the investigation period, after which custody must be purely judicial custody (jail).
layman_explanation: Under Section 187 BNSS, police custody can be granted up to a total of 15 days in whole or in parts during the initial 40 or 60 days of the investigation period, after which custody must be purely judicial custody (jail).

source_act: Section 187(3), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
user_query: What is 'Default Bail' (Statutory Bail) and when is an accused entitled to it?
legal_text_raw: If the police fail to file a final charge sheet within 60 days (for offenses punishable under 10 years) or 90 days (for death, life, or 10+ years), the accused acquires an absolute, indefeasible right to be released on Default Bail.

user_query: Can the police handcuff an under-trial prisoner while taking them to court?
legal_text_raw: Handcuffing is prima facie degrading and unconstitutional under Article 21. Handcuffs can only be used with prior recorded judicial permission if the prisoner is demonstrably violent, dangerous, or poses a severe escape risk.

source_act: Suresh Nanda v. CBI (Supreme Court of India)
user_query: Can police impound or seize a citizen's passport during an investigation?
legal_text_raw: No. The Supreme Court ruled that police can seize a passport temporarily under Section 106 BNSS, but CANNOT impound it. The power to impound or cancel a passport resides exclusively with the Passport Authority under the Passports Act, 1967.

source_act: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 & Delayed Registration Rules
user_query: What is the procedure if a municipal authority delays issuing a birth or death certificate beyond 21 days?
legal_text_raw: Births and deaths must be reported within 21 days. Beyond 21 days up to 30 days, registration requires a late fee. Beyond 30 days up to 1 year, written permission from the designated authority is required. Beyond 1 year, an order from an Executive Magistrate is required.
